newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS UPSET BY LARSSON IN INDIANAPOLIS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS UPSET BY LARSSON IN INDIANAPOLIS.

text.p: Pete Sampras had another gloomy encounter with a Swede Thursday when Magnus Larsson upset the world number one 7-6 (8-6) 4-6 7-6 (7-5) to reach the quarter-finals of the $1 million RCA Championships.
Sampras lost his first ATP Tour match since the quarter-final stage at Queens in early June, when he went out to Jonas Bjorkman, one of Larsson's Davis Cup teammates.

Sampras's 1997 hard luck with Swedes began at the French Open, when he lost to Magnus Norman, who celebrated a 21st birthday by dumping out the world number one. Sampras got his own back in the first round of Wimbledon with a victory over Mikael Tillstrom.

Sampras was displeased after the Indianapolis defeat which ended a 13-match win streak. "I didn't lose serve, that makes it a little disappointing," he said. "The balls were flying on me, it was frustrating.

"I didn't lose my serve once, this was a tough one to lose. But he has beaten me before and he was once number 10 in the world. I've just got to put this one behind me, take a few days off and go to the U.S. Open."

Larsson took control in the third-set tiebreaker, when he rolled out to a 6-0 lead. Despite multiple winning opportunities, Larsson needed six to finally triumph as Sampras saved the first five. A forehand into the net spelled the end for the American.

Crowd-pleaser and world number 74 Andre Agassi was to play at night against third seed Alex Corretja of Spain in hopes of continuing his comeback which began this week after seven first-round defeats.

Novak blocked more success for Sweden as he upset fourth seedd Thomas Enqvist 7-5 3-6 6-3. Bjorkman gave Sweden two men in the last eight with his win over Australian Todd Woodbridge, the seventh seed, 6-2 7-5.
Spanish fifth seed Carlos Moya stopped Australian Richard Fromberg 6-4 6-3, while 10th-seeded South African Wayne Ferreira beat Grant Stafford 6-4 7-6 (7-4).
